claims.text: The WTaTiVZr HEA is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each constituent.
The WTaTiVZr HEA has enhanced high-temperature plastic strain relative to commercially pure tungsten.
The WTaTiVZr HEA has enhanced high-temperature toughness relative to commercially pure tungsten.
Large atomic-size mismatches among W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr produce severe atomic-scale lattice distortions.
Severe lattice distortions impede dislocation motion and increase dislocation pinning.
Increased dislocation pinning produces greater work hardening in the HEA.
Lattice distortion activates additional dislocation-storage mechanisms during high-temperature deformation.
The resulting hardening and dislocation storage delay necking relative to pure tungsten.
The lattice-distortion-mediated dislocation response delays crack initiation and propagation under sustained high-temperature loading.
Under identical conditions at 1000–1500°C, the HEA will exhibit higher strain-to-failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical conditions at 1000–1500°C, the HEA will exhibit greater toughness than pure tungsten.
The deformed HEA will have a higher dislocation density than comparably tested pure tungsten.
The deformed HEA will show more pronounced slip-band interactions than pure tungsten.
The HEA will show local lattice-spacing heterogeneities consistent with dislocation pinning.
Producing both materials with comparable equiaxed grain sizes minimizes grain-size and grain-boundary differences.
Matched grain size, temperature, strain rate, and atmosphere provide a controlled comparison intended to isolate alloy-chemistry-related lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to tests at 1000–1500°C under controlled strain rates in an inert atmosphere.
Temperatures of 1000–1500°C are representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service.
Minor compositional segregation or impurities could contribute to the measured mechanical response.
Failure to observe both greater dislocation pinning and enhanced strain-to-failure and toughness in the HEA would falsify the proposed explanation.
